diff.shared_invariant: IMA step-index bytes are table indices after the block header has been accepted and cached predictor samples have been emitted.

hunks.role: admit the one-past mono step index in the IMA block header
store the trusted header index so the later nibble decoder uses it directly

edit_summary: Trust an IMA ADPCM mono step index that is exactly one past the 89-entry step table.
root_cause: The IMA ADPCM step index read from each block header must be within stepTable before it is kept in decoder state.
effect_path: Header byte 89 is accepted and stored, the initial predictor sample is returned from the cache, and the next nibble decode reads stepTable[pWav->ima.stepIndex[0]].
guard_p1: A valid DVI ADPCM/IMA mono stream has header[2] equal to 89; header[2] equal to 88 is the neighboring valid case.
guard_p2: The caller reads past the cached predictor frame into the compressed nibble payload.
hardness_reason: The cause is in block admission and state setup, while the out-of-bounds read is delayed until a later decode loop iteration.
naturalness_reason: Removing a redundant-looking clamp after weakening the matching validation is a realistic small refactor bug.
explanation: The IMA ADPCM step index read from each block header must be within stepTable before it is kept in decoder state. Header byte 89 is accepted and stored, the initial predictor sample is returned from the cache, and the next nibble decode reads stepTable[pWav->ima.stepIndex[0]].
boundary_case: Mono IMA ADPCM header step index is 89.
neighbor_case: Mono IMA ADPCM header step index is 88.
oob_site_expected: stepTable[pWav->ima.stepIndex[iChannel]] in the IMA nibble decode loop.
shared_invariant: The header validation and stored step index must agree that stepTable indices are strictly below drwav_countof(stepTable).

diff.shared_invariant: MS ADPCM predictor bytes are direct indices into the seven-entry coefficient tables on both block admission and nibble decoding.

hunks.role: admit the one-past predictor value when a mono block header is loaded
preserve the bad predictor until the delayed nibble decode table lookup

edit_summary: Accept the one-past MS ADPCM mono predictor value through both the block-header and delayed decode checks.
root_cause: MS ADPCM predictor bytes select coefficient-table entries and must be strictly below the table length.
effect_path: The mono block header stores predictor 7, cached header samples are emitted first, then the next compressed nibble reaches coeff1Table[predictor] and coeff2Table[predictor].
guard_p1: A valid mono MS ADPCM stream has a block predictor byte equal to 7; predictor 6 is the neighboring valid case.
guard_p2: The caller requests enough frames to drain the two cached header samples and decode at least one compressed nibble.
hardness_reason: The accepted index survives in codec state across cached-frame output before the table access in the nibble decode phase.
naturalness_reason: An inclusive/exclusive boundary regression on a codec predictor table is plausible and localized to format validation.
explanation: MS ADPCM predictor bytes select coefficient-table entries and must be strictly below the table length. The mono block header stores predictor 7, cached header samples are emitted first, then the next compressed nibble reaches coeff1Table[predictor] and coeff2Table[predictor].
boundary_invariant: coeff1Table and coeff2Table have indices 0 through 6.
boundary_case: Mono MS ADPCM predictor byte is 7.
neighbor_case: Mono MS ADPCM predictor byte is 6.
oob_site_expected: coeff1Table[pWav->msadpcm.predictor[0]] and coeff2Table[pWav->msadpcm.predictor[0]] in the mono nibble decode.
shared_invariant: The same predictor boundary must be enforced when the block is admitted and when deferred nibble decoding consumes the stored predictor.

diff.shared_invariant: Clearing an object must both release member storage and make every hash-table route to that storage unreachable.

hunks.role: keep freed member names in the item vector after json_object_clear releases them
keep hash cells pointing at the item-vector slots that held the freed names

edit_summary: Clear object members but keep hash cells and name slots pointing at the released key strings.
root_cause: json_object_clear must sever both the item-vector and hash-cell reachability paths after freeing member names.
effect_path: After json_object_clear frees each key, count is reset but the hash table still routes probes to item slots containing freed name pointers; a later json_object_set_value, json_object_get_value, or has-value call reaches strlen/strncmp on the released key.
guard_p1: A nonempty object is cleared with json_object_clear rather than destroyed.
guard_p2: The cleared object is reused for lookup or insertion before it is freed.
hardness_reason: The free occurs during a lifecycle reset, while the use is delayed until a separate public operation consults stale hash-table routing state.
naturalness_reason: Leaving stale hash-table routing after a logical clear is a plausible container lifecycle regression.
explanation: json_object_clear must sever both the item-vector and hash-cell reachability paths after freeing member names. After json_object_clear frees each key, count is reset but the hash table still routes probes to item slots containing freed name pointers; a later json_object_set_value, json_object_get_value, or has-value call reaches strlen/strncmp on the released key.
effect_site_expected: parson.c:577 json_object_get_cell_ix measures the freed key through a retained cell
conditional_expected: Positive clears and reuses the same object; negative destroys the object immediately after clearing or clears an object with no hash-table storage.
shared_invariant: A cleared object must not retain either item-vector or hash-cell reachability to released member names.
